Covers the code in `/home/zhengyew/telelean` as of this date.* ## Status in brief | | | |---|---| | **M1** (the board without AI) | **Done.** | | **M2** (one-shot "These suffice" with Claude) | **Implemented and integrated, but verified only with a scripted fake Claude (the FakeBackend).** Those runs used real Lean 4.35 and real clicks through the board in an isolated VS Code test instance. | **How to read this report.** - **Part 1** describes the architecture. - **Part 2** describes what a user can do today. - **Part 3** states the Lean logic precisely: the encoding, the statuses, the permitted set, the gate, and what is and is not guaranteed. - **Appendices:** - A: limitations and open items; - B: places where the docs and the code disagree; - C: glossary; - D: how this report was checked. --- # Part 1: Architecture telelean is a VS Code extension made of four TypeScript packages (npm workspaces). - **The Lean files are the source of truth.** Every card is an `@@ telelean v1` block inside a Lean comment. Every status is derived from Lean's output and never stored. - **All logic runs in the VS Code extension host.** Lean, git and Claude Code run as child processes of it. - **The board is a webview.** It displays what the host sends and turns gestures into typed messages. ## 1.1 The system in one picture ``` VS Code window ├─ board tab: webview (React, strict CSP) ⇅ typed messages (protocol v1), validated on both sides └─ extension host (Node in Electron), running dist/extension.js ├─ packages/extension thin adapter: commands, BoardPanel, BoardSession, CheckedEditApplier, watchers ├─ packages/runner ModelWorkspace · RunManager · LeanCheckEngine · shadow · ProposalService · llm/ │ └─ MCP tool server (HTTP on 127.0.0.1, per-run bearer token) ◀── telelean tool calls ───┐ └─ packages/core pure TS: markup, project model, edit planner, gate rules, protocol │ spawns: │ ├─ runLean: systemd-run scope → setpriv → keeper → bwrap → lake / lean / comparator │ │ (one Lean job at a time, process-wide) │ ├─ git (plumbing only): private refs in the model's repository; one bare repo per run │ └─ setpriv → claude -p --input-format stream-json … (cwd = the run's ws/) ─────────────┘ └─ PreToolUse hook: node telelean-path-guard.mjs (before every file-tool call) Model folder (opt-in: has .telelean/config.json) VS Code extension storage Model.lean, Model/.lean, Model//*.lean globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/-// .telelean/: config, layout, attic, attempts, ws/ build/ git/ session/ frozen/ gate/ run.json … decisions, graph.json; .lake/ ``` ## 1.2 Processes | Process | Started by | Role | Isolation | |---|---|---|---| | VS Code workbench (renderer) | you | editors and tabs; hosts the board's webview | VS Code's own | | Board webview (iframe) | `BoardPanel` | the React board: shows what the host sends and turns gestures into protocol messages; computes no Lean results | strict nonce CSP, no Node access, every message validated | | Extension host (Node in Electron) | VS Code, at activation | runs `dist/extension.js`, which bundles the extension adapter, runner, core, the MCP SDK and `diff`; serves the MCP tool server in-process | VS Code's own; workspace trust is required | | Lean/Lake jobs: `lake build`, `lake env lean --stdin --json` (check files, scratch checks), `leanexport`, `lake comparator` | runner, through `runLean` | builds, Lean facts, ghost and rendering checks, freeze exports, G4 | see below the table | | git | runner | history snapshots on private refs in the model folder's own repository; one bare repository per run | plumbing only; hooks, signing, gc and fsmonitor off; `GIT_*` redirections dropped | | Claude Code CLI (your binary, ≥ 2.1.295) | runner, when a run starts | the agent: `claude -p` in stream-json mode, with cwd = the run's `ws/`; its own session files go under `~/.claude/projects/` | own process group under `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`; tool allowlist; none of your settings; cleaned environment; subscription login only | | Path-guard hook `telelean-path-guard.mjs` | the CLI, before each file-tool call | allows or blocks the call by its path | runs with a real `node` when one is found (Electron in Node mode otherwise) | | VS Code Lean extension (not telelean's) | you | editor features; may build `.lake/` in the same folder | **not sandboxed**: it elaborates any file you open, accepted code included | **How `runLean` isolates a Lean job:** - a systemd user scope with `MemoryMax`, no swap and `OOMPolicy=stop`; - `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`; - a keeper shell; - `bwrap`: no network, `$HOME` hidden except a read-only `~/.elan`, sources read-only, `.lake/` writable, environment cleared; - fail-closed start: if any layer is missing, nothing runs; - one job at a time. ## 1.3 The four packages ### packages/core: pure TypeScript, shared by everything **Constraints.** It is compiled with `lib` ES2023 only, without DOM or Node typings. So it does no I/O and contains no LLM code. Its gate rules are the non-LLM judge of Claude's work. The other packages import its sources through path aliases; its `dist/` is unused. **Module groups:** - **Contracts** (marked FROZEN, additive changes only): - `model.ts`: cards, edges, graphs, derived statuses, vocabulary, Lean-check state; - `facts.ts`: `LeanFacts`; - `actions.ts`: BoardAction → EditPlan → FileChange, plus errors and undo/history types; - `run.ts`: runs, proposals and sidecar records; - `protocol.ts`: versioned host↔webview messages with hand-written validators; - `paths.ts` and `layout.ts`. - **`markup/`:** - a lexer faithful to Lean 4.35 and a declaration-header scanner; - the block parser, which reports TL0xx diagnostics and binds blocks (a pinned `lean:` beats adjacency); - a serializer and byte-preserving edits; - LeanOps: the D-11 rewrites and the D-9 docstring mirror. - **`project/`:** - `buildProjectModel` turns parsed files, hashes and facts into the project model: ids, bindings, ownership, vocabulary classification, statement closures, statuses with footprints, flags, TL1xx diagnostics and edges; - `subjectGraph` cuts out one subject's board. - **`edit/` and `kindChange.ts`:** - `planAction`, through an `EditSession` that re-parses between steps and keeps other cards' bindings; - `planKind` (D-11, using Lean facts); - the graph-only preview shown during a drag. - **`export/`:** `graph.json` format 1.1 and its JSON Schema. - **`gate/`** (M2): - the G0 token and file rules; - the ghost single-term rule; - the permitted set and the freeze snapshot; - `evaluateRules`: G1 errors read from facts, G3, G5, and the readiness and stage rules; - normalisation, ghost adoption, lifecycle edits, and plain-language findings. - **`proposal/`** (M2): the board diff, proposal labels, and codecs for `attempts.jsonl` and `decisions.json`. - **`samples/` and `graph.ts`:** the Spyro sample, a generated large graph, and M0 helpers the webview still uses. ### packages/runner: the Node engine (no `vscode` imports) **Foundation layers:** - **`lean/`**: M0's spike, now production code. - `runLean`, the only way a Lean-family process starts; - `sandboxProfile.ts` (the bwrap allowlist); - `toolchain.ts`: pins v4.35.0 and calls its binaries directly, never elan's proxies; - `leanNames.ts`: injection-safe generated names; - `shadow.ts`: copies that refuse symlinks; - `comparator.ts`: G4 (the freeze challenge, `leanexport`, `lake comparator`, classification of its verdicts); - `footprint.ts`: parsers for `lean --json` and `#print axioms`. - **`semantic/`:** - `refreshLeanFacts`, which turns a model root into `LeanFacts`; - `runExclusive`, the process-wide queue of one Lean job at a time; - the memory guard and `spawnMemoryMax`. - **`llm/`:** - the provider-agnostic `LlmBackend`/`LlmSession` interface with normalised events; - the five-tool `AgentToolHost` interface, with its zod schemas and reply renderers in `toolSchemas.ts`; - `ClaudeCliBackend`: binary lookup, environment stripping, path-guard confinement and its self-test, the subscription and hook preflight, the MCP tool server, and stream-json parsing; - `FakeBackend`: scripted steps through the same guard decision, schemas and renderers; - `StubToolHost`: M0's tool host, still used by the smoke script and tests. **M1/M2 machinery built on them:** - **`workspace/`:** `ModelWorkspace`. It scans and parses the model files, builds subject graphs, and runs the debounced, coalesced refresh. It owns the single queued write path (perform, undo, redo, revert, `applyChanges`) and the history. `initialize.ts` implements "Initialize Model Here". - **`shadow/`:** the run directory, the ws/→build/ sync by content comparison, the bare git repository written with `fast-import`, and the optional build seeding. - **`gate/`:** `LeanCheckEngine` (checkBase, check, freeze, normalise, gate, ghost check, statement rendering), plus findings and the scratch sources sent to Lean on stdin. - **`run/`:** `RunManager`. It owns: - the state machine, preflight and the backend factory; - the static system prompt and the context bundle; - the AgentToolHost and the caps; - the A2 gate loop, Feedback, ghost adoption and Accept; - persistence and recovery after a reload. - **`proposal/`:** - `ProposalService`: the proposed graph and its diff, changed files, statement and vocabulary reviews, definition questions, the lifecycle item, the report card, drift detection and Accept planning; - `files.ts`: the no-fuzz 3-way merge; - `DiskSidecarStore`: `attempts.jsonl` and `decisions.json`. **Build.** `tsconfig` is `noEmit`, so the runner is only type-checked. The extension bundles the runner's sources directly. ### packages/extension: the VS Code adapter (owns no model semantics) **`src/logic/`** (no `vscode` imports, unit-tested): - **`BoardSession`**, one per board. It keeps an edit FIFO queue and a separate run queue, so a run start or an Accept never blocks typing; cancel and read-only requests skip both queues. It coalesces publishes, switches subject when the shown one disappears, and adds the dependent cards to needs-confirmation answers. - **`actionMapping`:** protocol message → BoardAction. - **`editApplier`** (`CheckedEditApplier`). For each file it checks the current text against the planned before-text, writes minimal line edits in one WorkspaceEdit, undoes a partial apply, and saves. - **`changeBatcher`:** debounces events and recognises echoes of telelean's own writes. - **`modelPaths`:** keeps paths inside the root and refuses symlinks that lead out of it. - **`settings`:** clamps the `telelean.*` values. - **`runs`:** the consent texts, the lazy Claude backend factory (which refuses in Test mode) and the busy check. - Also initialize, restore, roots, groups, and the history and proposal previews. **`src/vscode/`:** - **`host.ts`:** the commands, one BoardPanel per root, restore after a reload, the consent modal, RunManager construction, and `TeleleanApi` with Test-mode hooks. - **`registry.ts`:** one ModelWorkspace and one RunManager per root, kept for the life of the window. Typing, saves and file-watcher events become invalidations, plus Lean refreshes while that root's board is open. - **`editor.ts`:** the WorkspaceEdit port, and a TextSource that reads open buffers first. - **`historyProvider.ts`:** read-only `telelean-history:` and `telelean-proposal:` diffs. - **`runner.ts`:** a replaceable record of the runner's factory functions. **`src/board/`:** `BoardPanel`. It runs the webview lifecycle, serves strict nonce-CSP HTML from `html.ts`, validates every inbound message with `core.parseWebviewToHost`, and queues messages until the session attaches. **Build.** esbuild produces one CommonJS `dist/extension.js`. The build copies the path guard to `dist/bin/` and checks that the bundle loads under a stub `vscode`. ### packages/webview: the board **Stack.** React 19, one zustand store and pragmatic-drag-and-drop. Vite 8 builds it into `packages/extension/dist/webview/`. There is no `index.html`: the extension writes the HTML. **Module groups:** - **`host/bridge.ts`:** the only caller of `acquireVsCodeApi`. It validates every incoming message with `parseHostToWebview` and forwards CSP violations, which `public/boot.js` records from page start. - **`state/store.ts`:** - updates the board optimistically (moves, re-orders, adds, edits, never deletes); - gives each request an id `r`; - `applyGraph` drops older graph versions, matches provisional cards, keeps the selection and rebuilds the proposal overlay. - **`model/`:** pure, unit-tested helpers. - **`board/`:** cards, columns, the Vocabulary group, ghost cards and drag and drop. `EdgeEngine` draws the arrows outside React from pure geometry. - **`header/`, `tray/`, `prompt/`, `dialogs/`, `toasts/`, `common/`.** - **`run/`:** RunPanel, Questions, Review, ReportCard, GhostSuggestion, ProposalBanner, RunBadge. **CSP discipline.** No style attribute anywhere (positions are set through the CSSOM), and colours come only from `--vscode-*` variables. ## 1.4 Main data flows ### 1.4.1 Refresh: how the board learns what Lean thinks 1. **Triggers.** The board opens; you save a model file; telelean edits; another program writes a model `.lean` file, `lakefile.toml`, `lean-toolchain` or `lake-manifest.json`; you click the badge or run the command. After a debounce (750 ms), triggers are coalesced into one refresh. 2. **`semantic.runExclusive(refreshLeanFacts)`**, in order: 1. the memory guard; 2. the toolchain and manifest checks; 3. hashing the sources; 4. `lake build Model` in place under `runLean` (sources read-only, `.lake/` writable, `.git` masked); 5. parsing Lake's log and computing module states; 6. reading the `.ilean` files (declarations, ranges, references) and the docstrings; 7. running one generated check file (`#check`, `#print`, `#print axioms`, `#check type_of%`) through `lake env lean --stdin --json`; 8. re-hashing, so that modules that changed meanwhile become stale. Lean and sandbox failures become statuses, and the last good facts are kept. 3. **Model and board.** `core.buildProjectModel` builds the project model. `subjectGraph(S)` cuts out the board, and the runner adds the attempts from `attempts.jsonl`. 4. **Publishing.** The runner rewrites `.telelean/graph.json`. BoardSession posts `graph` and `workspace` messages; the webview validates them and applies the graph. **Unsaved typing** is re-parsed after about 200 ms, through the TextSource that reads open buffers first, but it is not built. The affected cards show "changed since last check". ### 1.4.2 Edit, undo and history 1. **In the webview.** A gesture updates the store optimistically (deletes excepted), and the store posts a message with a request id. 2. **In the extension.** BoardPanel validates the message, BoardSession queues it, and `actionMapping` turns it into a BoardAction. 3. **`ModelWorkspace.perform`**, in one queue for the whole root: 1. `core.planAction` returns whole-file changes. Kind changes go through `planKind` with the Lean facts. When dependents must be confirmed, it answers `needs-confirmation` and lists them. 2. The layout and attic changes are materialised. 3. If you edited files by hand since telelean last wrote, a "Manual edits" snapshot is taken. 4. `CheckedEditApplier` writes the change (before-text check per file, one WorkspaceEdit, save). 5. An action snapshot is taken on the private refs, except for layout-only changes. 6. An in-memory undo entry is added (100 per subject). 7. The files are re-read, `graph.json` is rewritten, and a refresh is requested. 4. **The answer.** The webview receives an `actionResult`. It confirms the change, rolls it back with an error toast, or reopens the dependents or delete dialog. **Undo and Redo** apply stored patches with no fuzz (`fuzzFactor 0`). They refuse when the patch no longer applies, and they are snapshotted like actions. **History** works on private refs. Its operations: - list; - preview: a read-only multi-file diff opened beside the board; - revert: it snapshots first, and the revert itself can be undone; - prune. **Echoes.** `changeBatcher` suppresses the file events caused by telelean's own writes. ### 1.4.3 A run, end to end 1. **Start.** The tray sends `startRun`, which goes to BoardSession's run queue (separate from edits). Then come the busy check and the consent modal. Only a yes is remembered, per root, in `globalState`. 2. **Preflight.** `RunManager.start` checks, in order: - busy; - the selection; - the workspace; - the toolchain, a lakefile, and no Lake packages; - the sandbox; - free memory. Then the backend factory is built lazily: binary lookup and the `setpriv` launcher. 3. **Premises.** The premises declaration is an ordinary undoable action through `ModelWorkspace.perform`. It is skipped when unchanged, and for Self-evident?. 4. **Working copy.** `createRunShadow` writes the model and project files into `ws/`, as the board sees them (open buffers first), and into `build/`. It records a `base` commit in the run's bare repository and writes `run.json`. 5. **Base build.** `engine.checkBase` builds the user's files in the mirror. Lean errors end the run before Claude is contacted. Otherwise B's facts are saved to `base-facts.json`. 6. **Claude Code starts.** `ClaudeCliBackend.startSession`: 1. starts the MCP tool server; 2. writes the settings, hook policy and MCP config into `session/`; 3. self-tests the guard; 4. spawns the CLI; 5. checks that the account is a claude.ai subscription and that the CLI lists the guard hook as enabled. Then it sends the static system prompt and the first message (the context bundle). 7. **Tool calls** arrive over MCP at the RunManager's AgentToolHost: - `check_lean`, `freeze_statements` and `propose_assumption` go to `LeanCheckEngine`: G0 on the text against B, then (if clean) mirror sync, build and facts, then `core.evaluateRules` over B, A, R and S; - `ask_user` puts the run in "waiting for answer". The clock pauses, and the answers are recorded in `decisions.json`. 8. **Gate.** `finish(status)` triggers normalisation (a commit), then the gate: G0, G1, G3 and G5, plus G4 for `proved`. The outcome: - pass: a `gate-pass` commit; - fail: a notice on the board, and the exact findings go back to Claude; - at the attempt cap, after a second turn without `finish`, or at the turn or time cap: revert to the newest passing commit, normalise, and re-check (not counted). 9. **Proposal.** `ProposalService.build` produces the proposal, which the webview shows as an overlay with the review. A line is appended to `attempts.jsonl`. 10. **Your choice:** - **Accept** (1.4.4); - **Feedback**: a new round in the same Claude session; - **I hold this**: an `adopt` commit, a re-freeze, then a new round; - **Discard** or **Cancel**. When the run ends, old run directories are pruned (`telelean.run.keepRuns`). ### 1.4.4 Accept 1. **Precondition.** Every definition question must be answered "yes". 2. **No drift** (your model files are unchanged since the run started). - `planAccept` takes exactly the judged files plus the ticked lifecycle item. - `ModelWorkspace.applyChanges` writes them through the M1 path: snapshots, `CheckedEditApplier`, one undo entry, a history entry of kind `accept-proposal`, then a refresh. - No Lean check runs before applying. If no file changes, the outcome is only recorded. 3. **Drift.** 1. Your current files are written into `ws/` as an `accept-base` commit. 2. Claude's diff is merged onto them with 3 context lines and no fuzz; an overlap refuses the Accept. 3. A `rebase` commit is made, then normalisation and (for `proved`) a re-freeze. 4. The gate runs again with B := `accept-base`. On success, exactly the re-checked files are applied; any failure refuses the Accept. 4. **Afterwards.** A resolution line is appended to `attempts.jsonl` and the run ends. ## 1.5 What is stored where | Location | What | Written by | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Model folder: `Model.lean`, `Model/.lean`, `Model//{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean` | the cards (blocks in comments) and the Lean code | board actions and Accept, through the WorkspaceEdit path | in history; undoable | | `lakefile.toml`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | the project files | Initialize | the project history chain | | `.telelean/config.json` | the library name; it also marks the folder as a model (activation) | Initialize | project chain | | `.telelean/subjects//layout.json`, `attic/.lean` | card order; archived proofs | WorkspaceEdit path | in history; undoable | | `.telelean/subjects//attempts.jsonl`, `decisions.json` | run rounds and their resolutions; your answers to Claude | `DiskSidecarStore`, directly (temp file, then rename) | not in history, never undone | | `.telelean/graph.json` | export of the whole project (format 1.1) | the runner, directly | gitignored | | `.lake/` | the in-place Lake build | Lean jobs | gitignored | | `.telelean/frozen/`, `.telelean/sessions/` | nothing | (Initialize adds their `.gitignore` lines) | unused: runs live in extension storage | | The model folder's git repository: `refs/telelean//subjects/`, `…/project` | history snapshots | git plumbing; temporary files under `/telelean-tmp-*` | `` = the folder's path in the repository plus a short hash (`root` at the top level). Your branches, index, HEAD, remotes and hooks are never touched | | Extension-host memory | undo stacks (100 per subject), parse cache, current facts | runner | lost on window reload | | VS Code `globalState` | consent per root (`telelean.claudeConsent.`) | host | only a yes is stored | | VS Code `workspaceState` | board restore records (title, root, subject) | host | | | Webview state, per panel | subject, Vocabulary-group collapsed, request counter, run-panel size | webview | | | `~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/-//` | see below the table | shadow, engine, RunManager | the newest 10 finished runs per folder are kept | | `~/.claude/projects/` | Claude Code's own session transcripts | the CLI | used by `--resume`; never read by telelean | **Contents of a run directory:** - `ws/`: Claude's working copy; - `build/`: the Lean mirror, with its own `.lake/`; - `git/`: a bare repository; - `session/`: settings, guard policy and log, MCP config with the token, system prompt, `transcript.jsonl`; - `frozen//` and `gate//`; - `scratch/`: created but never written; - `run.json`, `base-facts.json`, `proposal-facts.json`. ## 1.6 Trust boundaries | Boundary | What crosses it | What protects it | |---|---|---| | Webview ↔ extension host | protocol-v1 messages |
  • strict CSP: two nonce'd scripts, no inline styles, no eval, local resources only from `dist/webview`
  • every inbound message is validated by core's parser, and the webview validates what it receives
  • Open in editor re-checks that the path stays inside the root, after resolving symlinks
| | Extension host → Lean/Lake | model sources (read-only); `.lake/` (writable) |
  • the `runLean` layers (1.2), failing closed
  • one job at a time, the memory guard, per-job time limits
  • Lean can run code while it elaborates (`#eval`, `initialize`), so the user's own files are sandboxed as well
| | Extension host ↔ Claude Code CLI | prompts, tool calls and results, file reads and writes in `ws/` |
  • your own unmodified CLI
  • tool allowlist (no shell, web or subagents), none of your settings
  • path-guard hook plus the CLI's own fences
  • `ws/` holds only model files
  • stripped environment; subscription-only checks
  • process group and death signal
  • per-round caps
| | CLI → MCP tool server | tool calls |
  • 127.0.0.1 on a random port
  • a per-run bearer token, compared in constant time
  • a Host-header check; browser Origins refused
  • config files with mode 0600
| | Claude's working copy → your files | proposal files |
  • the non-LLM gate (G0, G1, G3, G4, G5)
  • proposals are built only from judged commits
  • Accept needs definition approvals, goes through the recorded write path with before-text checks, and re-gates after drift
| | Your machine → Anthropic | cards, vocabulary, answers, any model file Claude reads, tool results, Claude Code's own telemetry |
  • per-folder consent, asked before anything is sent
  • no API key ever used
| | Other programs ↔ model folder | edits, Lake builds |
  • before-text checks on every write; echo suppression
  • Lake takes no build lock (see the trace caveat, 3.7 item 5)
| | The VS Code Lean extension | elaborates files you open, accepted code included |
  • nothing (outside telelean); workspace trust only
| **The trusted base.** It consists of: - Lean's elaborator, which produces the facts, and Lean's kernel; - `lake comparator`; - telelean's TypeScript decisions: binding, vocabulary classification, the permitted set, the gate rules, the G0 lexer, normalisation and the merge (details in 3.7 item 3). ## 1.7 Where the implementation departs from the original design These are departures from 02/03. Some were approved as amendments, others are still open. - **Claude backend.** The design's default was the Claude Agent SDK. The code drives your installed Claude Code CLI in stream-json mode instead (amendment A1); there is no Agent SDK dependency and no `telelean.backend` setting. - **Facts.** The planned compiled extractor (`telelean-extract`, with statement-closure hashes) was not built. M2 uses M1's approach: a check file plus `.ilean`. G5's "formal immutability" is replaced by text-and-printed-meaning comparisons, and closure hashes are deferred to H. - **Gate steps.** - G0, G1, G3, G4 and G5 exist. - G2 (`leanchecker` replay) is deferred to H. - G6 is not a gate step: flags appear in the review and report card, and certificates come in M3. - G1's per-declaration limits (10 s, 1.5 GB) are not implemented; only the per-job time limit and the memory cap apply. - **Shadow.** - It is a bare repository written with `fast-import`. The design had `git init` with a work tree, and so do the outdated comments in `shadow/types.ts`. - Runs build from scratch by default; the design copied `.lake/build`. - **Activation and settings.** Activation keys on `.telelean/config.json`, not `layout.json`. Several designed settings do not exist: `.backend`, `.sandbox.required`, `.review.pauseWhenRisky`, `.docstringMirror`, `.modelRoots`, `.exclude`. - **Verdicts.** The design allowed "insufficient" only with a countermodel. Today it is Claude's unverified claim, shown as "not proved". - **Run files.** They live in extension storage, not in `.telelean/frozen/` and `.telelean/sessions/` (Initialize still gitignores both). - **Live errors.** Error badges from VS Code's diagnostics (03 §5) are not implemented. Per-file summaries: docs/project-report-files.md --- # Part 2: Functionality and features This part says what a user can do with telelean today and what happens when they do it. **What it was checked against:** - the extension manifest and host; - the board; - the runner and core; - `docs/user-guide.md` and the last verifier's report. **Which code runs.** The bundles in `packages/extension/dist/` are newer than every source file. The extension is registered in place from `packages/extension`, so VS Code runs exactly this code. **Conventions.** Differences between the user guide and the code are marked **Docs vs code** and collected in Appendix B. Limitations and open items are in Appendix A. ## 2.1 Setting up and running ### 2.1.1 Requirements | Need | Details | |---|---| | Linux with the sandbox tools |
  • `bwrap`
  • a reachable systemd user manager (`systemd-run --user`, `systemctl --user`)
  • cgroup v2 with the memory controller
  • util-linux `setpriv`
All are in `/usr/bin` here. Picking one highlights it in the group; names outside the subject's vocabulary are greyed out as "elsewhere". **The Vocabulary group.** - **Place and state.** It is the first item of the Assumptions column and is collapsed by default. That covers its messages, questions and options, suggestions, summaries, and the glosses of new vocabulary. - **Theme colours.** Six colours can be overridden through `workbench.colorCustomizations`, with defaults for dark, light and both high-contrast themes: - `telelean.kindAssumption` - `telelean.kindDerivation` - `telelean.kindGoal` - `telelean.formalizedAura` - `telelean.vocabulary` - `telelean.highlight` The board follows VS Code's reduced-motion preference. ## 2.3 Editing the model without AI (M1) ### 2.3.1 Every board action | Action | Gesture | What is written | Undo / History entry | |---|---|---|---| | Add a card | A\|D\|G box | a comment block in `Model//Inbox.lean` | yes / "add" | | Edit the sentence | **Edit** or F2 (Enter saves, Esc cancels) | `natural_name:`. That text comes from the board's own cards only ("No card on this board uses it"). - **Re-planning with Lean.** The host re-plans the change with Lean's facts across the project. The host would accept a declare-only message, but the board never sends one. ### 2.3.6 Undo, Redo and History **Undo and Redo.** - 100 steps per subject, kept in memory. They survive closing the board, but not a window reload. - Tooltips name the action ("Undo: Add assumption: …"). - If you edited a file by hand since, Undo reverses only telelean's change, and refuses when that no longer applies ("changed since; use History to revert"). **History** needs git (amendment A3). Nothing is pushed. - **When snapshots are taken:** "Initial state" when a board first loads. Hand edits are snapshotted as "Manual edits" before telelean's next change. - **What a subject's snapshots cover:** its `.lean` files, its `layout.json` and its attic. `attempts.jsonl` and `decisions.json` are not covered. **The History dropdown.** - **Storage line:** "This subject: X · All subjects: Y". This is disk use, not memory. - **Entries:** "time · action · label", 50 at a time, with **Show older entries**. - **Preview** opens a read-only multi-file diff beside the board, titled `History:
notes:
I assembled the main report from the six package overviews, the features draft and the theory draft. All 21 fact-check corrections (C1–C21) and the 11 'missing' items (M1–M11) are applied in Part 3. I only read files: nothing was written to the repo or scratch, nothing published, no Lean run. Where to save it: docs/project-report-files.md already exists and calls itself the 'Appendix to docs/project-report.md' (2026-11-02), so the main report should be saved as docs/project-report.md. Part 1 ends with the requested pointer line.

Structure:
- Status summary.
- Part 1: architecture (new). Processes, packages, data flows (refresh, edit/undo/history, a run, Accept), storage table, trust boundaries, departures from the 02/03 design.
- Part 2: features, tightened. Old 2.7/2.8 moved into Appendix A, docs-vs-code consolidated into Appendix B.
- Part 3: Lean system, corrected.
- Appendices A (limitations/open items), B (docs vs code, from all surveys), C (glossary), D (how checked).

Features-draft errors I found by spot-checking the code and fixed:
- Root `npm run build` only type-checks the runner (`noEmit`). Core compiles to an unused `dist/`.
- The run's `scratch/` folder is created but never used; ghost checks are scratch files on Lean's stdin, not 'scratch projects'.
- The check file also uses `type_of%` and runs via `lake env lean --stdin --json`.
- A toast with Undo stays at least 10 s.
- The vocabulary flag 'new' and the 'broken' chip's flag are never set by core.
- The graph.json schema file is named 1.0 while the format is 1.1.
- Accept without drift runs no Lean check.
- After a revert, the proposal is the last passing commit plus normalisation. The re-check does not block.
- Only definition approvals gate Accept. 'Show the proof result now' exists.
